n: High-Value Goods (Art, Jewellery, Precious Metals, Luxury Vehicles)
ds: Purchase, trade and storage of portable, high-value assets, often with cash, to convert and store proceeds. Price subjectivity and confidentiality make valuation and origin hard to verify.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Art and Antiquities Market (2023)
FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risks and Vulnerabilities Associated with Gold (2015)
FATF, Guidance on the Risk-Based Approach for Dealers in Precious Metals and Stones (2008)

cn.rt: Luxury goods purchases funded by transfers, card spend or loan proceeds; unrelated-party payments and cash handled at branch.

rat: Dealers in art, jewellery, metals and luxury vehicles (DNFBPs) receive cash or wires from wealthy buyers; the goods are real assets held outside the bank.

ind.n: Cash or third-party payments for high-value items
ind.cx: Payments in cash, or from unrelated parties.
ind.fp: Cash sales are legal in some places.
ind.ds: High-value assets are bought with cash, crypto, third-party or otherwise non-standard funding.
ind.cn: High-value purchases paid in cash, crypto or non-standard funds

ind.cx: Price above or below a credible valuation.
ind.ds: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
ind.cn: Transaction price materially different from market value

ind.n: Buyer indifferent to quality, authenticity or price
ind.cx: Little interest in provenance or negotiation.
ind.ds: Customer readily accepts poor terms, fees, losses, penalties or prices, showing little interest in performance, provenance or negotiation.
ind.cn: Customer indifferent to cost, return or value

ind.n: Rapid resale or return for refund by cheque
ind.cx: Item bought then resold or returned for different payment form.
ind.ds: An asset is bought and quickly resold or returned for a refund in a different payment form, with no apparent reason or improvement.
ind.cn: Rapid resale or return of recently acquired asset

ind.n: Use of freeports or offshore storage and shell owners
ind.cx: Items held through opaque vehicles or storage.
ind.ds: Property, art, vessels or other valuables are acquired or held via a company, trust or storage arrangement with concealed beneficial owners.
ind.cn: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle

ind.n: Unclear provenance or sourcing of metals and stones
ind.cx: Gold or stones from unverified origin or recycled scrap.
ind.ds: Gold, metals or stones lack licence, assay or chain-of-custody evidence of origin, or are claimed as recycled scrap.
ind.cn: Unclear provenance of gold, metals or stones

ind.n: Vehicle purchased for cash and exported quickly
ind.cx: Luxury cars bought and shipped abroad soon after.
ind.ds: Luxury cars bought and shipped abroad soon after.
Assets, lifestyle spending or purchases clearly exceed the customer's known legitimate income or declared wealth, with no verifiable source.
ind.cn: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means

ind.n: Auction or intermediary used to obscure parties

ctl.ds: Prohibits or caps cash for purchases, loans, donations and settlement above a set value, requiring documented non-cash methods and threshold reporting for dealers. It removes a low-traceability payment route.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Obtains independent valuations, appraisals or comparable-sale evidence for high-value assets, collateral and traded goods, and escalates large variances. It reveals deliberately mispriced assets used to move or conceal value.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

Monitors specialised products such as insurance, securities, safe deposit and prepaid instruments for surrender, free delivery, overpayment, assignment, matched trades and unusual access. It catches product-specific abuse.

Requires refunds, cancellations and aborted-deal repayments to go back only to the original payer and method after validation of the request. It blocks the use of refunds to convert illicit funds into clean payments.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Applies enhanced checks to operators, counterparties, storage rationale and transactions that involve free-trade zones and free ports, including facility operator controls. It addresses the opacity and reduced oversight these locations can offer.

Maintains lists of higher-risk goods, species and commodity codes, tags relevant transactions and triggers extra documentary checks and screening of descriptions. It focuses scrutiny on the goods most associated with abuse.

Maps suppliers and sub-suppliers back through the chain, down to plot, mine or farm level where relevant, and requires traceability of key inputs to origin. It makes hidden high-risk sources visible so they can be excluded or audited.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

ctl.n: Agent and distribution network due diligence
ctl.ds: Vets, trains, caps and monitors agents, sub-agents and distributors who onboard customers or move funds on the institution's behalf, including quality visits, outlier analysis and disclosure of principals. It limits control failures at the edge of a distribution network.
